duration.from: Until siting and performance standards are developed and adopted; county page states a moratorium cannot continue indefinitely.
duration.to: Ran until siting and performance standards for data centers and cryptocurrency mining facilities were developed and adopted. The County Commission adopted a Data Center Standards section of the Morton County Land Use Code on 2026-09-10, satisfying that condition, per the county's own website.
duration.reason: The event that was to end the moratorium (adoption of siting and performance standards) occurred on 2026-09-10, per the county's own 'Data Center and Cryptocurrency Standards in Morton County' webpage.

legal_basis.to: Resolution 30-2024-03 (Sept. 12, 2024 moratorium). Superseded in substance by a County Commission resolution adopted 2026-09-10 (4-1 vote, Commissioner Tokach dissenting over a tonal-noise feasibility concern) that added a Data Center Standards section to the Morton County Land Use Code, following Planning & Zoning Commission review at its Feb. 25, March 25, April 22, May 27, and July 22, 2026 meetings, a subcommittee process (June-August 2026), and a P&Z recommendation of approval on Aug. 26, 2026.
legal_basis.reason: The county's own website, corroborated by KFYR-TV and the Bismarck Tribune, documents the full process culminating in the Sept. 10, 2026 adoption of permanent data-center standards.

current_status.to: Replaced as of 2026-09-23. The County Commission adopted a Data Center Standards section for the Morton County Land Use Code on 2026-09-10 (4-1), and the county's website states this final draft 'has been incorporated into the Morton County Land Use Code.' The standards set noise limits (noise-producing equipment generally at least three-quarters of a mile from an occupied home), require closed-loop cooling, and set setback, water/power-use, road, emergency-planning, and reclamation-bond requirements (with a waiver path if a former data center site is repurposed). Per the Bismarck Tribune's Sept. 11, 2026 report, the Planning & Zoning Director stated a separate notice period was required before the Commission could formally vote to lift the underlying moratorium resolution itself (since it was adopted by resolution), and she expected that vote at the Commission's next meeting after Sept. 10; no report of that specific repeal vote was found as of 2026-09-23. No data center application is currently pending in the county's own (non-extraterritorial) jurisdiction; a separate proposed Stark Power data-center/gas-generation project in north Mandan falls within the City of Mandan's extraterritorial area, not Morton County's jurisdiction.
current_status.reason: Reflects the Sept. 10, 2026 adoption of permanent siting and performance standards, which functionally replaces the 2024 moratorium's rationale, while noting the formal repeal vote on the moratorium resolution itself was still pending per the same reporting.

affected_projects.from: No specific application identified in captured county materials; the County's current page states no data center or cryptocurrency mining facility may be permitted until siting and performance standards are adopted.
affected_projects.to: No data center application is pending within Morton County's own jurisdiction. A proposed Stark Power data-center campus and natural-gas generation facility in north Mandan (which drew substantial public comment at county and city meetings) falls within the City of Mandan's extraterritorial area, so Morton County has no jurisdiction over that specific project.
affected_projects.reason: The Bismarck Tribune's Sept. 11, 2026 report identifies the one active-area project driving public interest and explains it is outside Morton County's own permitting jurisdiction, clarifying why the county's standards were adopted preemptively rather than to govern a specific pending application.

outcome.from: Draft standards were presented in February, March, and April 2026, but the county page states a public hearing will occur at a future Planning and Zoning Commission meeting.
outcome.to: Following P&Z review at five 2026 meetings (Feb. 25, March 25, April 22, May 27, July 22), a subcommittee process (June-August 2026), and a P&Z recommendation of approval (Aug. 26, 2026), the County Commission adopted the Data Center Standards section of the Morton County Land Use Code on 2026-09-10 by a 4-1 vote. The standards apply countywide and are not tied to approval of any specific project.
outcome.reason: Updates the outcome field to reflect the completed adoption, replacing the prior description of the standards as still in draft form.

evidence.supports: The county's own official statement that the Data Center Standards section was adopted by resolution on Sept. 10, 2026 and incorporated into the Land Use Code, plus the full drafting timeline.

evidence.title: Morton County approves new rules for future data centers
evidence.supports: Confirms the 4-1 vote and summarizes the noise, cooling, setback, and reclamation standards adopted.
evidence.quote: Morton County commissioners approved new rules for future data centers Thursday night on a 4-1 vote. The standards cover noise, cooling systems, setbacks and reclamation. ... County officials say no data center application is currently before Morton County.

evidence.title: Morton County Commission approves data center ordinance
evidence.supports: Confirms the 4-1 vote (Tokach dissenting over tonal noise), that a separate notice period and vote was still needed to formally lift the moratorium resolution, and that the Stark Power project driving public interest is in Mandan's extraterritorial area outside county jurisdiction.
evidence.quote: The data center ordinance passed 4-1, with Tokach voting against it because of the tonal noise issue. The commission considered voting to lift the county's moratorium on data centers and cryptocurrency facilities, but Planning and Zoning Director Natalie Pearce said a notice period was required as the moratorium was a resolution. Pearce said she expected the moratorium to come before the commission at its next meeting.

evidence.title: Morton County data center ordinance advances to commission
evidence.supports: Confirms the Planning & Zoning Commission's unanimous recommendation of approval and that the ordinance moved to the County Commission for a Sept. 10 vote followed by a 30-day public-notice/petition period.
evidence.quote: The ordinance now goes to the Morton County Commission for consideration on September 10. If adopted, it would then enter a public notice and 30-day petition period.

decisions.notes: The Bismarck Tribune article's body text is ROT47-obfuscated in the raw HTML/markdown archived (a known Lee Enterprises/BLOX CMS pattern); the quotes above were decoded from the saved source before citing, per this project's standard practice for such sources. Because the formal vote to repeal the 2024 moratorium resolution itself was still pending a notice period as of the latest reporting found (Sept. 11, 2026), 'replaced' is used here to reflect that the permanent standards this moratorium existed to produce are now adopted and in the code, consistent with the process guidance that adopted permanent regulations move a row to 'replaced'; a future pass should confirm whether the Commission has since taken the separate formal repeal vote.

Per the Oliver County Commission's own Feb. 10, 2026 minutes, the topic remained unresolved through that date: commissioners discussed that ordinances needed to be written, and voted to schedule a Feb. 26, 2026 Planning & Zoning public hearing on a new data center and cryptocurrency-mining facility moratorium (recommended at 90 days), with final approval to occur at the March County Commission meeting. The County Commission adopted Phase 3 on 2026-03-13.

evidence.title: Staff Report - Williams County Zoning Ordinance and Subdivision Regulations (Chapter 6-16 Data Centers)
evidence.supports: Confirms the exact June 20, 2023 moratorium date, the November 7, 2023 extension to Feb. 22, 2024, and the replacing Ordinance 2024-01-02.
evidence.quote: On June 20, 2023, The Williams County Board of County Commission instituted a 6-month moratorium for any permits for data centers to give the Williams County Planning and Zoning department time to review the current regulations and go back to the board with any recommendations. ... new_candidates.duration: Proposed two-year zoning moratorium on all industrial-scale development, including solar, wind, data centers, battery storage systems, electric transmission lines and gas-fired electrical generation facilities, to allow the township to update its zoning ordinances; not yet adopted
new_candidates.legal_basis: Not yet enacted. On 2026-09-22 the Township Board unanimously passed a motion (moved by Board Chair Dustin Burchill) to hold a formal public hearing on whether to adopt a two-year moratorium; the specific ordinance language has not been finalized
new_candidates.trigger: Geronimo Power (through affiliated LLCs including CCDC LLC) has purchase agreements for roughly 2,072 acres in Harmony Township and 934 acres in neighboring Durbin Township, and is pursuing a data center and a 200-MW battery energy storage system in the township in addition to an already-under-construction 200-MW solar facility (Harmony Solar); residents raised concerns about tonal noise, property values, water use, road traffic, organic-farming impacts, and inadequate study of impacts, and about a conflict of interest (a former township board chair who did not recuse himself from 2025-2026 zoning-ordinance votes had a pending land-purchase agreement with a Geronimo Power affiliate)
new_candidates.current_status: Pending as of 2026-09-23. The Township Board voted unanimously on 2026-09-22 to hold a public hearing on whether a two-year moratorium on industrial-scale development (data centers, battery storage, solar, wind, transmission lines, gas generation) is appropriate; no hearing date had been set. The board separately voted to seek a legal review of 2025-2026 zoning-ordinance amendments that eased approval conditions for the proposed data center, including whether a conflict of interest by a then-board-chair voids those amendments, and whether the pending conditional use permit applications for the data center and battery storage facility remain legally eligible for consideration pending that review.
new_candidates.affected_projects: A proposed Geronimo Power data center and a proposed 200-MW Harmony Storage LLC battery energy storage system in Harmony Township (Cass County); Harmony Solar, a 200-MW solar facility by Geronimo Power, began construction 2026-08-24 and is not itself blocked by the proposed moratorium's timing.
new_candidates.outcome: Board voted to schedule a public hearing on a proposed two-year moratorium and to seek a legal review of recent zoning amendments and pending conditional use permits before further action; no moratorium has been adopted yet.

evidence.title: Harmony Township Board to consider 2-year data center moratorium
evidence.supports: Confirms the 2026-09-22 unanimous board vote to hold a public hearing on a proposed two-year moratorium covering solar, wind, data centers, battery storage, transmission lines, and gas generation, and the related legal-review motion.
evidence.quote: Burchill made a motion, which passed unanimously, to hold a public hearing that would serve as a formal opportunity for people to comment on whether they think a moratorium is appropriate. The language he used in his motion ... was for a two-year zoning moratorium for all industrial-scale development including solar, wind, data centers, battery storage systems, electric transmission lines and gas-fired electrical generation facilities “in order to update its zoning ordinances to further protect the township and its residents.”

new_candidates.notes: This is a pending proposal only (a vote to hold a public hearing), not yet an adopted moratorium; classified enacted_status=pending per the research process guidance. A future pass should check whether the special meeting/public hearing has occurred and whether a moratorium was formally adopted.

new_candidates.date_enacted: First enacted in July 2025 (exact date not confirmed in sources reviewed); extended by County Commissioner vote on 2026-06-01
new_candidates.duration: A moratorium on the use of county-maintained roads for the transport and delivery of equipment and materials associated with wind turbine, solar panel, and related infrastructure construction; originally a 12-month term from its July 2025 enactment, extended by commissioner vote on 2026-06-01 (the length of the extension was not specified in the source reviewed)
new_candidates.legal_basis: McIntosh County Board of County Commissioners motion/action, first enacted July 2025 and extended by vote on 2026-06-01 (instrument/resolution number not located)
new_candidates.trigger: Commissioners raised concerns about the impact of large-scale wind and solar construction traffic on county-maintained roads and bridges (heavy loads, vehicles exceeding weight restrictions) after TransAlta announced and then dropped plans for a wind farm in the county; the county wanted road-use agreements and oversight in place before any wind or solar developer (including Orsted, whose Badger Wind Farm spans McIntosh and Logan counties) could use county roads for construction
new_candidates.current_status: Extended as of 2026-06-01 per the McIntosh Democrat; long-form reporting by Canary Media (2026-09) and Mother Jones (2026-09) independently describes McIntosh County as having 'adopted a one-year moratorium on new wind projects' in April 2026 -- a description that may refer to this same road-use moratorium (simplified) or to a distinct action not otherwise located in this pass. As of 2026-09-23 the road-use restriction on wind/solar construction traffic remains the confirmed, sourced instrument.
new_candidates.affected_projects: Badger Wind Farm (Orsted, 250 MW, spanning Logan and McIntosh counties) came online in January 2026 and is not affected (construction predates/was completed around the moratorium's operative window); the moratorium is framed as preventing any future wind or solar developer from using county roads without a road-use agreement.
new_candidates.outcome: A road-use moratorium restricting wind- and solar-construction traffic on county roads, in effect since July 2025 and extended by the County Commission on 2026-06-01.

evidence.title: McIntosh County Commissioners extend road moratorium on wind and solar projects
evidence.supports: Confirms the road-use moratorium, its July 2025 origin, its June 1, 2026 extension vote, and its scope (wind and solar construction traffic on county-maintained roads).
evidence.quote: The McIntosh County Board of County Commissioners voted Monday, June 1, to extend its moratorium on the use of county-maintained roads for the transport and delivery of equipment and materials associated with the construction of wind turbines, solar panels, and related infrastructure. The county's road moratorium was first enacted in July 2025 after commissioners raised concerns about the potential impact of large-scale renewable energy projects on local infrastructure.

evidence.title: Wind energy benefits North Dakota. So why has the pipeline dried up?
evidence.supports: Independently describes McIntosh County as adopting a one-year moratorium on new wind projects in April 2026, tied to Badger Wind Farm coming online and a second proposed Orsted project.
evidence.quote: Nevertheless, in April — a few months after Badger Wind Farm went online — McIntosh County adopted a one-year moratorium on new wind projects, citing concerns about how another Orsted project, proposed for the south part of the county, would impact nonparticipant property owners.

new_candidates.notes: Confidence is capped at moderate because of an unresolved discrepancy: the McIntosh Democrat (a local paper directly covering the county) describes a road-use moratorium enacted July 2025 and extended June 1, 2026, while Canary Media/Mother Jones (national outlets) describe an 'April 2026' moratorium on new wind projects generally. These may be the same instrument described with different framing/date precision, or two different actions; a future pass should check McIntosh County Commission minutes directly (mcintoshnd.com) to resolve which is accurate and whether a broader development (not just road-use) moratorium exists.
